About us

For over a decade, ezbob has pioneered the digital lending transformation of leading financial institutions worldwide. Because we understand the challenges and complexity of regulations, compliance, and IT we designed a proprietary Core Lending Platform that enables financial institutions to develop modular products on top of existing services while supporting the IT migration to digital services. The open platform enhances the current lending offerings and empowers the automation and scalability strategy by complementing the existing core banking platform. ezbob’s customers include Santander, Intesa SanPaolo, NatWest, and PayPal amongst others. The company is headquartered in London with offices in New York, Israel, and Bulgaria.

    A strong few days for Israeli #FinTech in the UAE. Together with our partners at the Israel Export Institute, we hosted last week eight innovative Israeli FinTech companies for a focused delegation across the UAE financial ecosystem. The companies met with leading regulators, financial free zones, banks and other key stakeholders, exploring opportunities across digital assets, tokenization, AI, financial automation and advanced banking technologies. For me, the value of these delegations goes beyond opening doors. It is about helping companies understand the market from the inside: the regulatory landscape, institutional priorities, where the opportunities are and what it takes to build meaningful partnerships in the UAE. The level of engagement throughout the delegation once again demonstrated the potential for deeper collaboration between the Emirati and Israeli FinTech ecosystems. Thank you to Sagi Itcher and Guy Kruger from our headquartered at Foreign Trade Administration - Ministry of Economy & Industry, for their support, and to our partners at the Israel Export Institute מכון היצוא, Nofar Moradian- Shiber and Shahar Branzburg, as well to Jitin Ladkani from our team at TradeIL UAE, for making it happen. Special thanks to Ambassador Yossi Shelley for hosting us for an insightful discussion on the Israel UAE economic relations, and to our Emirati partners for their time, openness and engagement. And of course, thank you to the eight Israeli companies that joined us and represented Israeli innovation in the UAE.     The FCA just published the most significant AI review in financial services anywhere in the world. The Mills Review doesn't call for new rules. Its message is sharper than that. As AI moves from recommending decisions to taking them, the firms that win won't be those with the most powerful models. They'll be those who can govern, explain and stand behind what they automate.     A credit decision can change the trajectory of a small business. A loan approved at the right moment. A mortgage that opens a door. Or a decline that sends someone away with no idea why and no path back. For years, the industry accepted that more powerful AI meant less transparency. You could have performance, or you could have explainability. Not both. That trade-off no longer holds. We've just published a deep dive into Explainable AI in credit risk and what it means for lenders navigating the EU AI Act, FCA Consumer Duty, and PRA SS1/23 all at once. The findings are worth sitting with: → XGBoost with SHAP explanation lands within 2 Gini points of the best black-box model — while meeting every current regulatory standard → Building for explainability actually improves your models, not just your compliance position → SHAP-based adverse action notices turn declined customers into recoverable ones → Open banking cash flow is the single highest-impact feature in SME credit models — by a clear margin Regulators have made their position clear. The institutions that treat explainability as a competitive advantage — not just a compliance checkbox — will be better positioned for what comes next. 📖 Full article: https://lnkd.in/eU7auEUG If you're thinking about how explainable AI fits into your lending strategy, we'd love to hear from you. Drop us a message or visit ezbob.com to start the conversation. #ExplainableAI #CreditRisk #Fintech #EUAIAct #FCAConsumerDuty #LendingTech #ResponsibleAI #ezbob #JohnChristiansen
